name: Subset Teaching Dimension / Littlestone Dimension (Incomparable)
details: Neither parameter admits a universal affine-linear upper bound in terms of the other on finite binary concept classes.
parameter_1_larger_witness: For $n\ge4$, let $\mathcal F_n$ consist of all singleton and doubleton subsets of $[n]$. Its STD is $n-1$, while leaf counting gives Littlestone dimension at most $\lfloor\log_2(n(n+1)/2)\rfloor$. The survey proves the complete minimum-teacher fixed point. Thus STD grows linearly while Littlestone grows at most logarithmically.
parameter_2_larger_witness: For the half-interval classes #classes/halfintervals with $n\ge2$, STD is one and Littlestone dimension is $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor$. The latter diverges with the former fixed.
proof_source: Proposition \ref{prop:subset-teaching-littlestone-incomparable} in the survey; half-interval endpoint values are database-owned.
references: \cite{zilles2011models} for the singleton--doubleton construction; the survey gives a direct fixed-point and tree-counting proof.
